summary.name: Screenize
summary.one_liner: Screenize is a free, open-source macOS screen recorder that automatically adds zoom, click effects, and keystroke overlays, with a multi-track timeline editor for adjusting them.
use_cases: recording software tutorials on a Mac
adding automatic zoom to screen recordings
free alternative to paid screen recording apps
summary.what_it_does: Screenize records a screen or window and tracks the cursor, clicks, and keystrokes in the background. It generates zoom keyframes automatically, using either a Continuous Camera mode that follows the cursor with spring physics or a Segment-based mode that plans zoom per activity such as typing, clicking, or scrolling. Click effects (ripple animations colored by left, right, or double click) and keystroke overlays are added automatically. All generated keyframes appear on a multi-track timeline with Camera, Click Effects, Cursor, and Keystroke tracks, where they can be edited and previewed before export. Export supports MP4 (H.264, H.265), MOV (ProRes), and GIF, up to 4K at up to 240fps, with saved presets.
notable: Automatic zoom generated from cursor and click data, fully editable on a timeline
Swaps the system cursor for 7 styles and adds gradient backgrounds, rounded corners, shadows, and padding
Built on native Apple frameworks including ScreenCaptureKit, AVFoundation, and CoreImage
Positioned as a free, Apache 2.0 alternative to Screen Studio, which costs $89+
caveats: Camera overlay is listed as planned, not available yet
Page compares against Screen Studio and is written by the project itself, so comparison claims are not independently verified
